notes:
Background: Orchid Retrospect manages a 12M-item media archive (press releases, long-form journalism, transcripts). Primary ask: enterprise-grade search for journalists and internal research teams with sub-200ms median query latency and predictable cost per query. They run nightly ingestion from S3 + on-prem tape restores.

Key constraints / callouts: 
- Very long documents (avg ~18k words, many 50k+). Chunking strategy is top concern: naive fixed-window leads to noisy retrieval and large index size.
- Target index size: ~8-12M chunks depending on chunking approach; budget ~ $0.02-$0.05 per end-to-end query (ANN + reranker).
- Must support regional data residency and customer-managed KMS for keys.
- On-prem install required for some customers; Redwood Private + VPC preferred.

Technical approach discussed: two-stage RAG pipeline. 
1) Sparse filter (title+metadata) + ANN over embeddings for candidate retrieval (top 200).
2) Cross-encoder reranker (fine-tuned) to reorder top 50 and produce final top 5.

Chunking experiments notes: 
- Fixed token windows: 1024 token chunks with 256 overlap produces high recall but index ballooned to ~14M chunks and retrieval cost high.
- Semantic paragraph chunking (split by semantic boundaries, min 300 tokens, max 1600 tokens) reduced index size ~20% and improved snippet coherence.
- Smart hybrid: paragraph-first semantic chunks + 1k fallback for very long flat documents (transcripts) gives best precision/recall tradeoff.
- Store chunk-level metadata: source timestamp, speaker, section headings to allow metadata filters and reduce reranker load.

Embeddings & reranker: 
- Embedding models in evaluation: lightweight 384-d open models (cost-effective) vs. 1536-d higher-quality models. Current POC uses 1536-d for initial ANN index and a smaller 384-d index for caching hot queries.
- Reranker: cross-encoder tuned on Orchid's annotated pairs (nDCG@10 target >0.62). Reranker latency SLO: p50 <120ms, p95 <350ms (they want p95 better but accept gradual improvement).
- Cost trade-offs: cross-encoder reranker is expensive per candidate; strategy is to limit to top 50 and use early-stopping heuristics when score gap > threshold.

Performance & ops: 
- QPS target: 30 sustained for internal research portal, bursts to 300 for newsroom spikes.
- Autoscaling policies need predictable GPU warm-up time; Redwood Dedicated sizing discussion in progress.
- Prefetch/caching: query result caching for repeated journalist queries; prefix/KV cache discussed for multi-turn re-ranking when follow-ups reference previous chunks.

Evaluation metrics & datasets: 
- Orchid provided a 4k-query eval set with human relevance labels (drive link above). Metrics tracked: nDCG@5/10, recall@50, latency p50/p95, cost per query.
- Initial baseline (open ANN + no rerank) nDCG@10 = 0.41; with tuned reranker rose to 0.59. Goal >0.65 with further reranker fine-tuning and smarter chunking.

- SLA language for reranker latency and regional failover.
